gen-gf-unica-one-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, which lets it hold the page steadily beneath Unica One's uniform strokes. Unica One's wide-eyed lowercase grabs attention, then the sans-serif body takes over.
gen-silkscreen-fs-bespoke-sans: Silkscreen is lo-fi retro, with space around every letter you can almost feel. Silkscreen's spaghetti lines do the playing, while Bespoke Sans, a sharp plain sans, does the refining with generous room between curve ends and stems.
gen-gf-warnes-manrope: Manrope keeps a bright open gap at every curve and barely any step between capitals and lowercase. Manrope stays quiet so Warnes, all tapering ink and stretched spacing, can earn its keep big and short.
gen-luckiest-guy-satoshi: Luckiest Guy is loud and cheerful, with ink that looks poured. Satoshi, a sans whose e never squeezes shut and whose x-height soars, would make paragraphs go down easily.
gen-megrim-switzer: A c as open as a bent paperclip gives Megrim its angular, futuristic edge. And while Megrim does the showing off, Switzer, a wire-like sans, does the approachable Swiss talking.
gen-mystery-quest-work-sans: Work Sans reads contemporary and modern, with c tips that never creep toward touching and a high mean line. Shrink Mystery Quest and its bookish, open-jawed curves get lost.
gen-dafont-blockletter-archivo: Sketchy but precise, Blockletter looks pencilled by a hand that never presses harder. Archivo, a sans-serif with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, gives that single-stroke sketch something sturdy and editorial to stand on.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-fs-asap: Raw and tactical, Capture Smallz comes with big-bodied lowercase. It makes the loud first impression, while Asap, a readable sans with open-arc c forms and near-capital body height, does the steady explaining.
gen-tourney-archivo: Wide tracking stretches every Tourney word, and its bulky, oversized small letters carry a single stroke width throughout. Tourney lands the punch, then Archivo's sans curves open outward to explain.
gen-tourney-fs-asap: Asap is a readable sans-serif whose c forms are open arcs and whose body height nearly matches the capitals. Against Tourney's pencil-like, never-thickening lines, that steadiness is the pair's whole appeal.
